artworks.title: Mercury and Battus
artworks.description: Jordaens' Boijmans canvas: Hermes tests the old herdsman who saw him drive Apollo's cattle — Battus bribed to silence, then turned to stone for speaking. Not Battus of Cyrene.

artworks.title: Mercury and Battus
artworks.description: Elsheimer's small panel of the Homeric Hymn / Ovid episode: Mercury confronts the Pierian witness of the stolen herd — Battus as the garrulous stone-to-be.

popCulture.title: Battus (mythology)
popCulture.description: Old forester who saw Hermes steal Apollo's cattle, took a bribe, and was petrified when he betrayed the secret — not the historical Battus I of Cyrene.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymns
popCulture.description: The Hymn to Hermes stages the cattle theft Battus witnesses — the archaic frame for the bribe-and-stone tale.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses (Mercury and Battus)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's telling (Met. 2): Hermes returns in disguise, re-bribes Battus, and turns the oath-breaker into a touchstone.
